evidence.M1: Every claim is pinned to a specific event/scene (e.g., ev-032/sc-148 for Neo's denial, ev-025/sc-115 for Morpheus's sacrifice) and the grounding paraphrases name what in the scene supports it.
evidence.M2: Questions are welded to this story's mechanics — 'a wager on a man rather than a prophecy' (ev-032), the red pill as literal switch (ev-010), Smith 'pronouncing' a fate Neo refuses (ev-039) — not transplantable abstractions.
evidence.M3: The dilemma's horns are mutually exclusive and each costed in events: Morpheus models sacrifice (ev-025) and Cypher models self-preservation (ev-020, ev-029), with Neo's 'not the One' making the gamble carry no guarantee.
evidence.M4: Coverage spans the full event layer from Trinity's opening capture (ev-001) through the Sentinels overrunning the deck (ev-046), including secondary arcs like the Sentinel hunt (ev-019) and Cypher's betrayal (ev-020–029).
evidence.M5: One over-reach: the 'WE (group)' stance claims the crew pays 'the price of the sacrifice horn,' but the layers show the crew as 'doubters and believers' (ev-016), not willing self-sacrificers — sharpening ambiguity into a claim the layer doesn't fully support; otherwise nothing is invented.
evidence.M6: All five throughlines hold distinct positions on the dilemma: THEY (cut the loss, ev-031/032/040), I (refuse the arithmetic, ev-032/038), YOU/Morpheus (sacrifice as destiny, ev-025/031/035), WE/Neo-Trinity (loyalty overrides survival, ev-032/044), and WE-group (Cypher vs. the believers, ev-016/020/029).

commentary: The artifact is exceptionally grounded and story-specific, with a genuinely costed central dilemma and disciplined, distinct perspectives. The only flaw is a single interpretive over-reach in the society perspective that reads the crew's doubt as active self-sacrifice, which the event layer frames as a split between doubters and believers rather than a collective living of the sacrifice horn.
